item.research_question: How can intrinsically stable single-atom Pd catalysts be fabricated on high-entropy supports to overcome sintering challenges under high-temperature conditions?
item.material_system: High-entropy fluorite oxides (CeZrHfTiLa)Ox (HEFO) and Pd1@HEFO (0.5–2.0 wt% Pd loading)
item.processing_route: Mechanical milling of metal salt precursors (Ce, Zr, Hf, Ti, La, Pd) with fumed silica followed by pyrolysis at 900 °C in air for 4 h, and subsequent etching of silica with 2.5 M NaOH for 8 h at room temperature
item.test_conditions: CO oxidation activity measured via light-off curves; hydrothermal stability tested at 750 °C for 10 h in 10 vol% H2O/N2; thermal stability tested at 900 °C; DOC activity at GHSV of 200,000 mL gcat−1 h−1
key_findings: Pd1@HEFO exhibits an onset temperature for CO oxidation of ~80 °C, compared to 223 °C for Pd@CeO2.
Complete CO oxidation for Pd1@HEFO occurs at 170 °C, whereas Pd@CeO2 requires 253 °C.
The apparent activation energy (Ea) for Pd1@HEFO is 43.40 kJ/mol, significantly lower than 72.21 kJ/mol for Pd@CeO2.
CO chemisorption determined 6.44% surface Pd atoms (0.0644 μmol CO/μmol Pd), confirming isolated Pd sites.
The ratio of surface chemisorbed oxygen (Oβ) to lattice oxygen (Oα) in Pd1@HEFO is about twofold higher than in Pd@CeO2.
Pd1@HEFO retains structural integrity and single-atom dispersion after hydrothermal treatment at 750 °C for 10 h.
Post-deposition Pd/HEFO-p sintered and aggregated after treatment at 900 °C, unlike the mechanochemically synthesized Pd1@HEFO.
item.mechanism: The formation of (PdyCeZrHfTiLa)Ox solid solution is an entropy-dominated process where high configurational entropy decreases Gibbs free energy, stabilizing isolated Pd atoms within the HEFO sublattice via Pd–O–M bonds. This structure enhances the reducibility of surface lattice oxygen and creates oxygen vacancies, facilitating the Mars–van Krevelen mechanism for CO oxidation.
item.limitations: Pd atoms in Pd1@HEFO are not stable in reductive atmospheres (e.g., H2 treatment), making the catalyst more suitable for oxygen-rich conditions like diesel exhaust oxidation.
item.future_work: The authors suggest this entropy-driven methodology may guide the development of next-generation single-atom catalysts.
quotes: Here, we report a novel entropy-driven strategy to stabilize Pd single-atom on the high-entropy fluorite oxides (CeZrHfTiLa)Ox (HEFO) as the support by a combination of mechanical milling with calcination at 900 °C.
The formation of (PdyCeZrHfTiLa)Ox solid solution is an entropy-dominated process, whereas the decreased configuration entropy induces the dissociation of (PdyCe)Ox as an enthalpy-driven process.
Pd1@HEFO has an Ea value of 43.40 kJ/mol, which is much lower than that of Pd@CeO2 (72.21 kJ/mol), further identify the advantage of Pd1@HEFO catalyst.
